summary: Two new destinations proposed (King Island, Flinders Island), 14 spots placed inside them, 0 standalone. Strzelecki National Park merged as a container.

new_destinations.name: King Island
new_destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:King Island (Tasmania) (island centre; reference only, confirm)
name_evidence: Discover Tasmania 'Guide to King Island' (tourism brand page)
new_destinations.reason: Seven kept spots (Cape Wickham Lighthouse, Currie, Cataraqui, Calcified Forest, Seal Rocks, Martha Lavinia Beach, King Island Historical Museum); a Bass Strait island visitors fly to and base on. Farthest spot Cape Wickham is ~31 km from the centre, within 75% of a 70 km span. Proposal only: needs description, reasons, tips, months, header (Pipeline C).

new_destinations.name: Flinders Island
new_destinations.coordinates_source: wikipedia:Whitemark (the island's main town and hub; reference only, confirm)
name_evidence: Discover Tasmania Flinders Island guide (tourism brand page)
new_destinations.reason: Seven kept spots (Strzelecki Peaks, Trousers Point, Wybalenna Chapel, Killiecrankie to The Dock Coast Walk, Killiecrankie Bay, Castle Rock, Furneaux Museum); Strzelecki National Park is a container and not counted. Spots lie within ~35 km of Whitemark. Proposal only.

spots.name: Cape Wickham Lighthouse
spots.coordinates_source: resolve-pin HIGH: OSM man_made=lighthouse (-39.588547,143.942981) and Wikipedia article agree within 10 m; recorded point is the Cape Wickham State Reserve node, same place
spots.reason: Island's headline sight; 2 counted sources, 1438 views; on the north-west cape, 38 km from Currie, inside the island span.
spots.bio: Australia's tallest lighthouse, 48 m, built in 1861 after the Cataraqui wreck, with climbing tours.

spots.name: Currie
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: Photon place=town node, within 130 m of the Wikipedia article point (-39.931111,143.850556); a town-centre point, acceptable for a town spot
spots.reason: The island's main harbour town with its own draws (harbour, visitor centre); its museum is kept as a separate spot because it is a distinct attraction. Currie Lighthouse is a review candidate, not placed.
spots.bio: King Island's main harbour town, with the visitor centre, the harbour and the old lighthouse keeper's precinct.

spots.name: Cataraqui
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: Photon historic=memorial 'Cataraqui Memorial' (507 m from the Wikipedia wreck point -40.027139,143.880444); the memorial is where visitors stand; confirm against the Maritime Trail brochure
spots.reason: Skeptic keep; Maritime Trail headline stop; 4652 views. Memorial and wreck site on the south-west coast, 12 km from Currie.
spots.bio: Memorial and wreck site of the 1845 barque Cataraqui, Australia's worst peacetime maritime disaster.

spots.name: Calcified Forest
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin found no OSM feature; take the Great Short Walk's route midpoint from the managing agency's map
spots.reason: Two counted sources (Wikivoyage, Discover Tasmania); short Great Short Walk, a distinct natural feature.
spots.bio: A 30-minute, 1.3 km Great Short Walk through limestone formations left by a calcified forest about 7000 years old.

spots.name: Seal Rocks
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin found no feature; take the lookout car park from the managing agency
spots.reason: Skeptic keep despite short visit; one counted source; lookout on the island's highest cliffs, start of the Copperhead Track.
spots.bio: Lookout on the island's highest cliffs, about 60 m above the sea, reached by a short walk.

spots.name: Martha Lavinia Beach
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin returned only a track and lake 3 km away (Lake Martha Lavinia); beach is on the north-east coast; needs the beach's own OSM natural/beach or Wikipedia point
spots.reason: Skeptic keep: one source, second-tier beach named for surf and beachcombing; inside the island span.
spots.bio: North-east coast surf beach, rated among the world's best breaks by Surfing Life, good for beachcombing.

spots.name: King Island Historical Museum
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: Photon tourism=museum 'King Island Museum' (single geocoder feature of the right type, ~530 m from the Currie hint); confirm
spots.reason: Skeptic keep: one source; museum in the old lighthouse keeper's cottage at Currie with its own exhibits (not a wrapper for the town).
spots.bio: Museum in the old lighthouse keeper's cottage with shipwreck and sealing history and the original Cape Wickham lens.

spots.name: Strzelecki Peaks
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin found no feature; pin the middle of the walk from the agency route map
spots.reason: Headline summit walk, 3 counted-source park; Great Short Walk inside Strzelecki National Park (container, merged).
spots.bio: Steep 4-5 hour return walk to the 756 m summit of Mount Strzelecki, the island's highest point.

spots.name: Trousers Point
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin found no feature; take the Trousers Point car park from the agency
spots.reason: Headline beach and Great Short Walk, 2 counted sources; inside Strzelecki National Park (container, merged).
spots.bio: Turquoise beach with a Great Short Walk loop, snorkelling and a walk-in campground at its southern end.

spots.name: Wybalenna Chapel
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: Wikipedia article point for Wybalenna Aboriginal Establishment; resolve-pin found no OSM feature; confirm chapel position
spots.reason: Kept: listed 'Don't miss' by Discover Tasmania and Wikivoyage; accessible chapel and cemetery; 11465 views.
spots.bio: Chapel and cemetery at Wybalenna, the 1830s-40s settlement where Aboriginal Tasmanians were exiled.

spots.name: Killiecrankie to The Dock Coast Walk
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin offered only the Commons median at Killiecrankie; pin the middle of the route from the agency map
spots.reason: Kept; the single spot for the walk, with Stackys Bight, Old Man's Head and The Dock folded in (those are rejected as parts).
spots.bio: Rocky coastal walk from Killiecrankie to The Dock, past a sea arch at Stackys Bight and Old Man's Head.

spots.name: Killiecrankie Bay
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: only a Commons photo median near Killiecrankie; needs the bay's own beach feature
spots.reason: Kept: topaz ('Killiecrankie diamonds') fossicking, a Discover Tasmania 'Don't miss'; the town itself is rejected as a wrapper.
spots.bio: Bay where visitors search the sand at low tide for semi-precious topaz, known as Killiecrankie diamonds.

spots.name: Castle Rock
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin found no feature; pin the middle of the walk from the agency route map
spots.reason: Kept, second-tier Great Short Walk named by Discover Tasmania; a separate walk, not the park itself.
spots.bio: Beach-hop walk to towering Castle Rock, one of Tasmania's 60 Great Short Walks.

spots.name: Furneaux Museum
spots.coordinates_source: LOW: resolve-pin found no feature; the museum is at Emita, take its point from the operator or OSM
spots.reason: Kept: two counted sources with distinct exhibits.
spots.bio: Island history museum at Emita, with a muttonbirding shed replica, police cells and a Sydney Cove anchor.

container_not_listed.name: Strzelecki National Park
container_not_listed.reason: Kept (3 counted sources) but it is a container of Strzelecki Peaks, Trousers Point and Castle Rock, so it is not listed beside its parts. It has only 3 spots so it does not clear the 4-spot bar as its own destination, and it is not a spot of another park; it is described in Flinders Island's description (entry charged per vehicle) and its walks are spots of Flinders Island.

standalone_neighbour_check: No standalone spots exist, so none lies within 40 km of either proposed destination. The two islands are ~400 km apart and their spans do not overlap.
notes: All Tasmania entries use timezone Australia/Hobart; no copy names a source.
Most pins are LOW from resolve-pin and were left null or provisional with needs_research including 'coordinates'; Pipeline C must resolve them before apply (no memory pins).
Hours, cost and ticketUrl are null for every spot and flagged in needs_research.
Spot ids are new: no king-island or flinders-island id appears in src/data or its history.
Cross-region: nothing in this region is owned by another Tasmanian region.
